headline: Towable weakness, higher taxes drag results; dividend rises
summary_short: Fiscal Q3 2026 (quarter ended April 30, 2026) revenue fell 3.9% y/y to $2,781.5M as North American Towable net sales dropped 24.6% on a 25% unit-shipment decline; net income fell 28.1% to $97.2M as gross margin compressed and the effective tax rate rose to 28.4% from 13.9%.
summary_long: NA Towable led the decline (net sales -24.6%, gross profit -$84.6M) on a 25% unit-shipment drop, while NA Motorized grew 7.7% and Europe rose 11.8% (mostly FX). Gross margin fell on unfavorable mix and higher material costs; SG&A fell 3.1% on lower incentive comp. Other income rose $55.6M on asset-sale gains and fair-value marks, partly offsetting the operating-income drop. Effective tax rate jumped to 28.4% from 13.9%, pushing net income down more than pretax income. Cash fell to $371.9M (from $586.6M at July 31, 2025) after YTD dividends and buybacks. The Board raised the quarterly dividend to $0.52/share and repurchased $50.5M of stock this quarter, $298.5M remaining under the authorization. No formal forward guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: NA Towable unit shipments fell 25% on weaker dealer demand, only partly offset by NA Motorized (+7.7%) and Europe (+11.8%, mostly FX). Net sales include a $72M FX tailwind.
Decline driven by lower consolidated net sales plus a lower gross margin from unfavorable NA Towable/European product mix toward lower-margin units and higher material cost inflation.
Gross profit compression was only partly offset by a 3.1% cut in SG&A (lower incentive compensation from reduced pretax income).
Pretax income fell less steeply than net income because the effective tax rate rose to 28.4% from 13.9% on jurisdictional earnings mix and last year's non-taxable FX gains not recurring.
EPS fell slightly less than net income (-26.5% vs -28.1%) because weighted-average diluted shares fell ~1.8% y/y from buybacks.
NA Towable dealer destocking (independent dealer inventory -13.7%) drove the miss; Motorized and Europe held up. Board raised the dividend to $0.52/share and kept repurchasing stock.
